fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. Jesus goes away once more and prays a third time. His first prayer was in verse 39, the second time in verse 42, and now this one. Three trips away to pray, and the text keeps count.
That's right, baker. He prays a third time, “…saying the same thing.” The text gives no new words this time. His earlier prayer ended with “…may Your will be done.” (Matthew 26:42).

That's right, baker. Jesus says, “Rise, let us go! See, My betrayer is approaching!” He tells them to get up first, and then He points out that the betrayer is coming. The scene is about to change fast.

That's right, baker. Judas, one of the Twelve, arrives “…accompanied by a large crowd armed with swords and clubs…” The text says they were sent from the chief priests and elders of the people. He didn't come alone.
The text doesn't mention shepherds, friend. It says Judas, one of the Twelve, arrives with a large crowd armed with swords and clubs. That's the crowd the text describes. Staffs aren't on its list.

The text doesn't mention tax collectors, baker. Judas, one of the Twelve, comes with “…a large crowd armed with swords and clubs…” The text says they were sent from the chief priests and elders of the people. That's who is behind them.
That's what Jesus says, friend. He tells the companion, “Put your sword back in its place…” and then explains, “For all who draw the sword will die by the sword.” He answers him directly.
Yes, baker. The text says, “Then all the disciples deserted Him and fled.” I think this one hurts, so I won't dress it up. It's right there in the passage, as the last line of the scene.
